objections.claim: `asProducerId(v: unknown): ProducerId` / `asContractRevisionId` return non-nullable branded types, so on invalid input they must either throw or return a value that is not actually valid. The spec never says which. On the ledger path this is a behavior regression: `verifyAuthLeg` currently tolerates malformed records (a `null` `producer_id` flows into `deriveKey` as `Buffer.from(String(null))` and the HMAC simply fails, recorded as a failure), and the CLI paths currently emit a clean exit-2 on missing/empty flags. A throwing validator turns both into unhandled exceptions on exactly the malformed-data paths the audit leg exists to classify gracefully.
objections.evidence: spec §3 "Branded ids" defines the validators with a non-nullable return and no failure contract; `commissaire.js` `verifyAuthLeg` iterates ledger entries and calls `deriveKey(gov.master_secret, e.producer_id, e.contract_revision)` with no throw path today; the spec's DONE mandates re-minting "every `producer_id`/`contract_revision` reaching `deriveKey`" through these validators.
objections.predicted_consequence: a hand-corrupted or partially-written `declared-effects.jsonl` (the exact input `audit verify` / `governance-check` are built to inspect) crashes the audit with a stack trace instead of returning `{ pass: false, failures: [...] }`, and an empty `--producer` flag crashes the CLI instead of the documented exit-2.

objections.claim: The brand-flow mechanism rests on `const producerAuth: ProducerAuthApi = require("./producer-auth")` in `commissaire.ts`. But `require` returns `any`, so the assignment is an unchecked `any`→interface conversion, and nothing — not `tsc`, not the cast-prohibition check (which only scans `as`/`<T>` nodes) — verifies that `ProducerAuthApi` matches the runtime `module.exports` object. If a developer adds a method to `module.exports` without extending the interface, `commissaire.ts` loses type coverage on that method; if the interface declares a method the runtime lacks, `commissaire.ts` compiles cleanly and crashes at runtime with a `TypeError`. `export =` (which would tie the shape) is banned by `erasableSyntaxOnly`, and the spec does not require the available fix (`module.exports = { ... } satisfies ProducerAuthApi`, which is erasable and legal).
objections.evidence: spec §3 "Source module shape" mandates the typed `require` pattern and bans `export =`; `producer-auth.js`'s `module.exports` is a flat object of ten members that the new `ProducerAuthApi` interface must mirror by hand; the cast-prohibition check's scope is explicitly `AsExpression`/`TypeAssertionExpression` only.
objections.predicted_consequence: the first post-conversion edit that adds an export to `producer-auth` without updating `ProducerAuthApi` ships a `commissaire.ts` that type-checks, passes `regions check`, and fails at runtime — the exact class of mistake the conversion claims to move to compile time.

objections.claim: The DONE requires the committed emit to be "byte-stable across two consecutive builds", but that is only guaranteed within one `node_modules` install. `typescript ~5.9` resolves to the latest 5.9.x patch on each fresh `npm install`; a patch release that changes emit output makes the committed `.js` stale on the next clean checkout, and the freshness gate that would catch it is deliberately deferred to FAFF-1171.
objections.evidence: spec §3 "Toolchain" pins `~5.9`; §8 DONE requires byte-stability; §2 OUT OF SCOPE defers the CI freshness gate to FAFF-1171; the Open Questions section punts the exact patch.
objections.predicted_consequence: a contributor on a newer 5.9.x patch runs `npm run build`, gets a different emit than the committed one, and either commits a spurious diff or ships a stale emit — the exact divergence the ratified sequencing says FAFF-1171 will detect, but which this slice's own byte-stability DONE cannot guarantee.

objections.claim: The check's allow-list (`asProducerId`, `asContractRevisionId`, "any sibling `as<Brand>` validator") must be hand-extended for every future validator, and a developer who adds a validator without updating the allow-list breaks the build — while the typed-`require` seam (`const producerAuth: ProducerAuthApi = require(...)`) is itself an unchecked `any`→typed conversion at a cross-module boundary that the check structurally cannot see. The check therefore enforces the letter of the cast ban while the spec's own sanctioned pattern violates its spirit.
objections.evidence: spec §3 "Cast-prohibition check" defines the allow-list and the AST-node scope; §3 "Source module shape" mandates the typed `require`; the check is a new bundled script with no existing lint infrastructure to inherit.
objections.predicted_consequence: the first slice that converts an outer importer (`cli-surface`, `governance-check`) must extend the allow-list and re-verify the typed-`require` pattern, and any validator added without an allow-list edit fails CI with a confusing "cast at boundary" error pointing at the sanctioned mint site.

objections.claim: The cast-prohibition check collects only `AsExpression`/`TypeAssertionExpression` nodes whose target type is a *branded* type (`ProducerId`/`ContractRevisionId`/`OpaqueId<…>`). A `value as any` at an input boundary is not collected, and `any` is assignable to `ProducerId`, so the S2 TS2345 guarantee ("a raw string / un-minted `any` reaching `deriveKey` is a `tsc` error") does not fire either. The spec's own design principle — "no bare `as`/`<T>` crosses these [boundaries]" — is therefore bypassable with a one-token, check-passing construct (`flags["--producer"] as any`), and the same gap applies to casts to a type *alias* of a branded type (`type Foo = ProducerId; value as Foo`), which the check's "to a branded type" matching is not specified to resolve.
objections.evidence: Spec §3 "Cast-prohibition check — Chosen (mechanism defined)" — "collect every `AsExpression` … to a branded type (`ProducerId`/`ContractRevisionId`/`OpaqueId<…>`)" and "fails on any such node whose enclosing function is not on the allow-list"; §3 "Brands flow at every boundary" — "a `string`/`any` reaching `deriveKey` un-minted is then a `tsc` error (TS2345)" — but `any` is assignable to `ProducerId`, so `as any` defeats both the AST check and `tsc`.
objections.predicted_consequence: A developer can write `producerAuth.deriveKey(master, flags["--producer"] as any, …)` and both the cast check and `tsc` pass, so the compile-time guarantee the whole conversion is built on is weaker than advertised. The runtime HMAC/Ed25519 cores still fail-closed on a genuinely wrong value, so this is not a runtime exploit — but the mechanism does not enforce its own DONE line ("no `as`/`<T>` crossing a boundary"), and the check's type-matching is underspecified for aliases.

objections.claim: The DONE item requires a fixture that "proves a raw string / un-minted `any` passed to `deriveKey` in `commissaire.ts` fails `tsc` with TS2345", but the spec never states how the fixture is built, how it is compiled (same tsconfig? a separate one?), or how the test asserts the failure (non-zero exit vs. grepping the specific TS2345 error code). A fixture that fails for an unrelated reason (syntax error, missing module, a different type error) satisfies a naive non-zero-exit assertion while proving nothing about the brand flow. The fixture is also a *copy* of `commissaire.ts`, not the real file — the DONE's "in `commissaire.ts`" phrasing is inaccurate, and the fixture proves only that a synthetic violation is caught, not that the real code is clean (which is S4a's job, and S4a only catches the ledger path if the record fields are pinned to `string` — the spec never states the field types, so a record pinned as `{ producer_id: any }` would satisfy "pinned (not `any`)" while making the DONE's consequence claim "an un-minted `any` reaching `deriveKey` is a `tsc` error" false).
objections.evidence: DONE item "A negative-build fixture proves a raw string / un-minted `any` passed to `deriveKey` in `commissaire.ts` fails `tsc` with TS2345 (S2)"; scenario S2 "A dedicated negative-build fixture asserts this. [holdout]"; DONE "the parsed ledger/admission record types in `commissaire.ts` are pinned (not `any`)".
objections.predicted_consequence: A build ships a fixture that exits non-zero for any reason (or a minimal repro that never touches the real `commissaire.ts`), the test passes, and the DONE is claimed — a reviewer cannot distinguish a genuine TS2345-on-the-real-path proof from a vacuous one.

objections.claim: The DONE item asserts `commissaire.ts` "validates every input boundary … with no `as`/`<T>` crossing a boundary", but the named enforcement (S3's `check-no-boundary-cast.mjs`) collects only `AsExpression`/`TypeAssertionExpression` nodes *to a branded type* (`ProducerId`/`ContractRevisionId`/`OpaqueId<…>`). A cast to any other type at a boundary — `JSON.parse(raw) as EffectDescriptor`, or `as any` — is invisible to the check. The spec's own principle ("pinned to its type by a runtime validator, never by a bare `as`/angle-bracket assertion at the boundary") is broader than the check, so a build can pass S3 and the check while violating the DONE item and the principle.
objections.evidence: DONE "`bin/lib/commissaire.ts` validates every input boundary … with no `as`/`<T>` crossing a boundary"; S3 "collect every `AsExpression` … and `TypeAssertionExpression` … node to a branded type"; §3 principle "never by a bare `as`/angle-bracket assertion at the boundary".
objections.predicted_consequence: A build with `as any` or `as EffectDescriptor` at the stdin/ledger boundary passes the check (exit 0) and S3, yet the DONE item "no `as`/`<T>` crossing a boundary" is false — the AC is not enforced by the mechanism the spec names, so it cannot be decided from the check alone.

objections.claim: `producer-auth.ts` does not invoke `producerAuthSelftest()` at module load (it defines and exports it), so "runs directly" cannot simultaneously mean `node producer-auth.ts` (which exits 0 without running the selftest — trivially satisfied by any loadable file) and "its `producerAuthSelftest()` exits 0" (which requires an unspecified wrapper invocation). Separately, the new `package.json`'s `type` field is never pinned: if the build agent sets `"type": "module"`, Node 22.18+ type-stripping treats `producer-auth.ts` as ESM and `require("node:crypto")` crashes at runtime, failing S4c — the AC is decidable but not guaranteed by the spec's stated inputs.
objections.evidence: DONE "`producer-auth.ts` runs directly (its `producerAuthSelftest()` exits 0) under Node 22.18+ type-stripping"; scenario S4c; §4 step 1 (package.json contents unspecified on `type`).
objections.predicted_consequence: The build agent either ships a trivially-passing "file loads" check that never exercises the selftest, or sets `"type": "module"` and fails its own AC — in both cases the DONE item's pass condition is not what the spec text describes.

objections.claim: The DONE item "A clean-install smoke on Node 20 runs `faff commissaire --selftest` … from a marketplace-style copy … with no `npm install`" is decidable, but no scenario covers it. The closest scenario, S4b, runs the selftest against the in-tree emit on Node 20 — it does not exercise the copy-without-`node_modules` path, which is the ADR-0132 install path the DONE item exists to prove.
objections.evidence: DONE "A clean-install smoke on Node 20 runs `faff commissaire --selftest` … from a marketplace-style copy"; scenario S4b "Selftests pass on the emit lane".
objections.predicted_consequence: A build whose in-tree selftest passes but whose copied artifact fails (e.g. a stray absolute path, a missing file in the copy set) satisfies every scenario yet fails the DONE item, and no scenario would have caught it.

objections.claim: "`faff commissaire --selftest` startup recorded on this ticket for source and emit" is satisfied by any recorded numbers — there is no threshold, no comparison, and no assertion. As an acceptance criterion it is vacuous: a build that records "source: 500 ms, emit: 500 ms" (or records nothing beyond a placeholder) satisfies it.
objections.evidence: DONE "`faff commissaire --selftest` startup recorded on this ticket for source and emit (spike baseline: plain JS 95 ms, `.ts` 227 ms, bare `node -e 0` 73 ms)".
objections.predicted_consequence: The DONE item is marked complete regardless of the measured values; it cannot be failed, so it does not function as a verifiable acceptance criterion.

objections.claim: The DONE requires `faff regions check` to exit 2 when any `bin/lib/*.ts` lacks a `.js` sibling, but `regionSources()` returns `.js` files only, and the spec never states how `regionsEmitCoverage` discovers `.ts` files. If it is wired with the `.js`-only source set, it never sees a `.ts` file and the guard is vacuous. S6's test is the enforcement, but the wiring that makes the guard fire is left to the build agent.
objections.evidence: DONE "`regions.js` exports `regionsEmitCoverage`; `faff regions check` exits 2 when any `bin/lib/*.ts` lacks a committed `.js` emit"; §3 "add `regionsEmitCoverage(files)` to `regions.js`"; `regionSources()` in regions.js lists `.js` only.
objections.predicted_consequence: A build wires the guard over the `.js`-only set, the S6 test is written against a hand-constructed fixture that bypasses the real wiring, and the guard never fires on the real tree — the DONE is claimed while the protection is absent.
